title: The Clockmaker's Shop
synopsis: Otto Brandt fixes clocks in the old Hart Building, where Eleanor made her toys.
He was at Grand Central, and at the bench on the bridge.
Is the grumpy clockmaker the one racing you?
goal: Find out why Otto wants the Lark and where he went on Sunday.

options.label: He wants to sell it.
options.feedback: Read it again. What does Otto say about money?

options.label: He wants to show it on TV.
options.feedback: Otto never talks about TV. Where does he want the Lark?

options.label: He thinks it belongs in the Hart Building.

notes: Letter: Otto's angry letter to Dr. Brooks. His reason (the Lark belongs at home, not money) makes him a suspect with a motive, and also shows he is not greedy.

clueInputs.note: An old clockmaker sat on the bench at nine.

play.title: Otto's Letter
story: On Bleecker Street stands an old brick building.
Above the door, an iron bird is cut into the stone.
Dr. Brooks meets you there with a letter in his hand.
play.letterIntro: Otto's letter to Dr. Brooks says:
play.letter:
Dear Dr. Brooks,
The notebook was found in the attic of MY building.
Eleanor Hart made her toys here. She taught my grandfather, Karl.
Her Lark belongs here, where she made it.
I do not want money. I want it home.
— Otto Brandt
play.question: Why does Otto want the Silver Lark?
hints: Find the line that says where the Lark belongs.
Read the line about money. Does he want it?
play.successMessage: You know why Otto wants the Lark!
transition: Otto wants the Lark back in the Hart Building.
"He was very angry," Dr. Brooks says.
Inside, a hundred clocks are ticking.

clue.title: Otto's Reason

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene) in Otto's shop: his diary is on the desk; the photo wall opens once it is read. The three islands of New York Harbor are told apart by what stands on them (a tall green lady with a torch, a red-brick hall with four towers, a round stone fort).
Otto's plain boots by the door (a note) are paid off in Case 06: the star prints are not his.
The choice pictures reuse one place picture (liberty_island, Case 06) and add two (ellis_island, island_fort), all 1536x1024.

Coordinates measured on the made clock_shop.png (1536x1024, sha256 defcaf8a…) with a 50px grid sheet (season_factory). The diary lies open on the desk left of centre (its area is the desk top and drawers, not the chair); the three photos hang one above another on the right wall, above the workbench.

play.title: Otto's Diary
story: Otto is out. His shop door is open.
"He never locks it," says the baker next door.
Clocks tick on every wall. You look around carefully.
play.letterIntro: Otto's diary is open on the desk:
play.letter:
Sunday
8:30 AM — Fixed the old clock in the bridge tower office.
9:00 AM — Sat on Eleanor's bench. Said hello to her brass bird.
9:30 AM — Took the ferry to see my sister.
She sells postcards on the island of the tall green lady with a torch.
play.question: Where did Otto go after the bridge?
hints: Find Otto's diary on the desk and read it first.
Look at each island on the photo wall. Which one has a tall green lady with a torch?
transition: The tall green lady is the Statue of Liberty.
At 9:30, Otto took a ferry to Liberty Island.

play.title: The Tiny Screws
story: The door bangs open. Otto is back!
"What are you doing in my shop?" he shouts.
Maya holds up a brass screw. "Is this from the bench?"
play.letter:
The bench had four screw holes.
Each hole is as wide as a finger.
Otto's brass screws are as small as grains of rice.
A screw that small would fall right through the hole.
play.question: Could Otto's screws come from the bench? Finish the sentence.
play.prompt: Otto's screws are too ____ for the bench's holes.
hints: Compare a finger and a grain of rice.
Could a grain of rice fill a hole as wide as a finger?
play.successMessage: The screws are not from the bench!
transition: "They are clock screws, from the bridge tower clock!" Otto snaps.
"I said hello to that bird. I did not take it!"
But Otto still looks at you like a cat at a mouse.

feedback.BIG: Is a grain of rice bigger than a finger? Read again.
feedback.LARGE: Is a grain of rice bigger than a finger? Read again.

play.orderFeedback: Check your spelling. It is a short word.

intro: Greenwich Village. Small streets, old trees and brick houses.
In 1926, Eleanor Hart made her toys in the Hart Building.
Today, Otto Brandt fixes clocks there.
play.caseSummary: Otto wants the Lark home, not money. He sat on the bench at nine. Then he took the 9:30 ferry to Liberty Island. His screws are clock screws, not the bench's. His boots have no stars. Karl's photo shows Eleanor, baby Ruth and a violin.

notes: Act 2 opens on the red herring: Otto has a reason and was at the bench, but his reason is not money, his screws are not the bench's and his boots are plain.
Karl's old photo (s4_ep05_e4): a violin beside Eleanor's daughter, paid off in Case 08.
